documents.title: New Patient Visit and Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 32F, here to establish care. Moved her primary care here after her old office stopped taking new appointments for months at a time. Teaches second grade in town.

No active complaints. Hay fever every spring and again in late summer since high school: sneezing, itchy watery eyes, runny nose. Gets through it without anything; has not wanted a daily pill. No asthma.

PMH: seasonal allergic rhinitis. No surgeries. No hospitalizations.
Meds: none.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
FHx: mother has generalized anxiety; father with high blood pressure and high cholesterol; one younger sibling, healthy.
Social: never smoked. Doesn't drink at present, no drug use. Single, lives in an apartment on Pleasant St.

ROS otherwise negative.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT: TMs clear, nasal mucosa a little pale, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no adenopathy or thyroid enlargement. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities no edema. Skin no rashes. Neuro grossly intact. Mood and affect normal.
PHQ-9: 1.

A/P
1. Preventive care: baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH. One-time HIV and hepatitis C screening, she agrees. Tdap today (last tetanus she can recall was in her teens). Flu shot when the clinic gets supply in October. Pap per old records, will request them.
2. Seasonal allergic rhinitis: mild, she prefers to ride it out. Revisit if it starts interfering with sleep or work.

RTC 1 year, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Trauma Surgery Discharge Summary
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional trauma center, Trauma Surgery service
Admitted 01/10/2020, discharged 01/14/2020
Patient: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987
Allergies: NKDA

Admission diagnosis: Motor vehicle collision, multiple injuries.

Discharge diagnoses:
1. Mild traumatic brain injury (concussion)
2. Right femur fracture, status post open reduction and internal fixation 01/10/2020
3. Blunt abdominal trauma, diagnostic laparoscopy negative 01/10/2020

Hospital course: 32-year-old woman brought in by EMS after a severe collision. Hemodynamically stable throughout. Imaging showed a closed right femur fracture. CT head without intracranial injury; clinical picture consistent with mild TBI. Given the mechanism and concern for intra-abdominal injury, taken to the OR with general surgery for diagnostic laparoscopy, which showed no solid organ or hollow viscus injury, followed by orthopedics for open reduction and internal fixation of the right femur the same evening. Mechanical and pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis while inpatient. Mobilized with PT on hospital day 1, weight bearing as tolerated on the right with a walker. Tolerating diet, pain controlled on oral agents, incisions clean.

Neuro at discharge: alert and oriented, no focal deficits. Concussion precautions reviewed.

Discharge medications: acetaminophen 500 mg tablet, 1 tab every 6 hours as needed for pain.
No other home medications.

Disposition: home with family support. Walker. Outpatient physical therapy referral sent.
Follow-up: orthopedic clinic in 2 weeks for wound check; primary care within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Discharge Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Discharge summary from the trauma center received yesterday. Called pt. She is home, mother staying with her this week. Getting around the apartment with the walker. Pain manageable with Tylenol. Incisions dry, no fever. No headache or vomiting. PT eval set up for next week. Booked with PCP Tues 1/21; mother will drive her.

conditions.label: History of mild traumatic brain injury

documents.title: Hospital Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Trauma center discharge summary reviewed in full.

Collision 1/10. Admitted 1/10 to 1/14: mild TBI with a clean head CT, right femur fracture with ORIF the night of admission, and diagnostic laparoscopy for blunt abdominal trauma that was negative.

Today: one week out of the hospital. Using the walker, weight bearing as tolerated. Pain at the thigh incision mostly at night, Tylenol a couple of times a day is enough. No headaches since discharge, no vomiting, no confusion; her mother has not noticed anything off. Sleeping OK. Starts PT Monday. Out of work for now; school is covering her class.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Comfortable sitting. Lateral right thigh incision healing well, staples in, no erythema or drainage. Calf soft, nontender. Small laparoscopy port sites clean. Abdomen soft, nontender. Neuro nonfocal, gait with walker steady.

A/P
1. Right femur fracture s/p ORIF: per ortho. Wound check with them next week. PT.
2. Mild TBI: doing well, no post-concussive symptoms today. Reviewed what to watch for. Gradual return to screens and work.
3. Blunt abdominal trauma, negative laparoscopy: nothing further.
4. Med rec: acetaminophen PRN only.

Work note given through 2/14, to be revisited with ortho. Call with any headache, new weakness, calf swelling or shortness of breath.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Ms. Whitcomb is under my care following a hospitalization and is unable to work through February 14, 2020. Her return date will be reassessed with her orthopedic surgeon.

documents.title: Orthopedic Follow-up Letter
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
Orthopaedic Trauma Clinic
Date of visit: 04/28/2020
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987
Allergies: NKDA

Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Whitcomb on 4/28, about 15 weeks after open reduction and internal fixation of her right femur fracture. She finished her course of outpatient physical therapy last week and is walking without an assistive device. She reports no thigh pain.

Exam: well-healed lateral thigh incision. Full knee and hip range of motion. Quadriceps strength 5/5. Gait normal, no limp. Neurovascularly intact distally.

Radiographs of the right femur at the visit: fracture healed with bridging callus, hardware intact and in good position, no loosening.

Assessment: healed right femur fracture after ORIF.
Plan: no restrictions, full activity. Home exercise program. Hardware may stay unless it becomes symptomatic. Follow up with us as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in her care.
Orthopaedic Trauma Surgery

orders.reason: trauma-related nightmares, flashbacks and anxiety after January car crash

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home, identity confirmed, consents to telehealth.

She wrote last week asking to talk about how she's been since the crash in January. Leg fully healed, walking normally.

But since the accident: nightmares most nights where she is back in the car, wakes terrified. Flashbacks during the day. Anxious most of the time. She has not driven since January; gets rides or walks. Car horns or a siren outside make her extremely anxious and she has to stop what she's doing. Remote teaching this spring has made it easier to hide. Not drinking, no substances. No thoughts of self-harm or of not wanting to be alive. Mother has an anxiety disorder; she has never been treated for anything like this herself.

GAD-7 15. PHQ-9 7, item 9 zero.

Obs on video: anxious, coherent, linear, good eye contact.

A/P
Trauma-related symptoms for ~5 months after the January collision; picture strongly suggests PTSD. Discussed that this is common after an injury like hers and very treatable. She wants an evaluation and is interested in therapy first. Referral to psychiatry placed; front desk to help with first available. Gave crisis line number. Check in after she's seen.

documents.title: Psychiatry Consultation
documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry
Date of service: 07/07/2020
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987, age 32
Referred by: primary care
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Reason for referral: nightmares, flashbacks and anxiety after a motor vehicle collision.

History: Ms. Whitcomb is a 32-year-old elementary school teacher who was seriously injured in a car crash in January of this year (mild TBI, right femur fracture repaired surgically, negative laparoscopy). Over the six months since, she has had recurring nightmares in which she relives the crash, waking with overwhelming fear and a sense of helplessness. She has intrusive flashbacks during the day. She has avoided driving entirely and becomes acutely anxious at the sound of car horns or sirens. Anxiety is present most of the day. She denies suicidal ideation, psychotic symptoms or manic symptoms. No prior psychiatric history or treatment.

Past medical: seasonal allergic rhinitis; mild TBI and femur ORIF 01/2020; diagnostic laparoscopy 01/2020, negative.
Family: mother with generalized anxiety disorder; father with hypertension and hyperlipidemia; younger sibling healthy.
Social: teacher, single, lives alone. Never smoker. No current alcohol; denies any substance use history.

Vital signs within normal limits.
Mental status / exam: casually dressed, restless in the chair, shifting frequently. Startles visibly when a door closes in the hallway. Speech normal rate. Mood "on edge". Affect anxious, congruent. Thought process linear; no SI/HI; no perceptual disturbances. Insight and judgment good.

Labs drawn today: CBC, TSH and basic metabolic panel all within normal limits.

Assessment: Post-traumatic stress disorder following the January 2020 collision.

Plan:
- Trauma-focused psychotherapy: cognitive processing therapy with one of our therapists, weekly; intake scheduled.
- Psychiatry follow-up in about a year, sooner if needed.
- Safety planning reviewed.

Thank you for this referral.
Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Psychiatry visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Abigail, I got the letter from psychiatry. Glad you were able to get in and that therapy is lined up. Their blood work was all normal. Let me know how it's going, and we'll catch up at your physical this fall.

documents.title: RE: Psychiatry visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. First therapy session is next week. Nervous but hopeful.

She says the nightmares are less frequent, maybe once or twice a week now, and she can hear a siren without leaving the room. Still not driving. Back in the classroom in person this fall, hybrid schedule.

No headaches, memory or concentration complaints from the TBI. Allergies were a nuisance in August as usual.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing. HEENT normal. Neck no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Right thigh scar well healed; normal gait. Neuro nonfocal. Affect mildly anxious, appropriate.
PHQ-9 6, item 9 zero.

A/P
1. PTSD: improving with CPT. Continue with psychiatry/therapist.
2. History of mild TBI: no residual symptoms.
3. Allergic rhinitis: seasonal, untreated by choice.
4. Health maintenance: flu vaccine today. Labs last year normal, none needed. Pap 2017 normal, due 2022.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual.

PTSD after the January 2020 crash: she had a good stretch through last winter after CPT, nightmares rare by the end. Then in January of this year she was robbed at gunpoint in her own neighborhood. Did not seek any medical care. Was OK for a while, but since about July the nightmares and flashbacks are back, now of the robbery, and she goes out of her way to avoid a few streets near her apartment. Jumpy, on edge, hard to concentrate grading. Says she feels far away from her friends and family, even her mom. No SI, no substances, no alcohol.

She has not been back to psychiatry since last year and wants to go back; she will call them this week. She was due for a psychiatry follow-up anyway.

Otherwise well. Completed COVID series in the spring. Seasonal allergies as usual in August.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, a bit guarded. HEENT normal. Neck supple. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Extremities no edema, right thigh scar healed. Neuro nonfocal.
PHQ-9 9, item 9 zero.

A/P
1. PTSD with recurrence after a second trauma (armed robbery 1/2021): she is reconnecting with psychiatry and her therapist. Offered to place a new referral; she doesn't need one, still established there. Crisis resources reviewed.
2. Allergic rhinitis: no change.
3. Health maintenance: flu vaccine today. COVID booster when eligible as an educator. Pap due next year.

RTC 1 year or sooner.

documents.author: psychiatry
documents.body:
Outpatient Psychiatry, follow-up
Date of service: 01/03/2022
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987, age 34
Allergies: NKDA. Current medications: none.

Ms. Whitcomb was evaluated here in July 2020 for PTSD after a motor vehicle collision and completed a course of cognitive processing therapy with good response. She returns now after a second trauma: in January 2021 she was mugged at gunpoint near her home. About six months later her symptoms returned, and for the last six months she has had recurrent nightmares, flashbacks and avoidance of parts of her neighborhood. She describes feeling keyed up, having trouble focusing, and startling easily. She has felt cut off from friends and family. No suicidal ideation. No alcohol or substance use.

Vital signs within normal limits. Physical examination normal.
Mental status: well groomed, cooperative, mood "wound up", affect anxious and somewhat constricted, thought process goal directed, no SI/HI, no psychotic features, insight good.

Assessment: Post-traumatic stress disorder, recurrence of symptoms following a second traumatic event.

Plan:
- Resume trauma-focused psychotherapy (CPT) with her therapist here, weekly, now addressing the robbery as well.
- Psychiatry follow-up in about a year, sooner as needed.

Thank you for your continued involvement in her care.
Outpatient Psychiatry

documents.title: Psychiatry note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Abigail, I saw the note from your psychiatry visit last week. Glad you're back in therapy. Reach out any time if things get harder in between.

documents.title: RE: Psychiatry note
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you, I will. It helps knowing you all talk to each other.

documents.title: Wanted you to know
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi. I wanted to let you know I was in another car accident on June 24. I was in the passenger seat, my friend was driving and she died. I only had minor injuries and didn't go to the hospital. I've already called my therapist and I'm seeing her weekly again. I'm not sure what I need from you, I just didn't want you to hear it later.

documents.title: RE: Wanted you to know
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Abigail, I am so sorry about your friend. Thank you for telling me. I'm glad you reached out to your therapist right away. If anything isn't healing, or you're not sleeping or eating, let me know and I'll see you sooner than September. If you ever feel unsafe, call 911 or go to the nearest ED.

Patient: Abigail Whitcomb, 38F, DOB 09/01/1987
Allergies: NKDA. Home medications: none.

CC: dizziness

HPI: 38-year-old woman with PTSD, a history of mild TBI from a car crash in 2020, and seasonal allergic rhinitis. About a week ago she blew her nose very forcefully and right away felt the room spin, with nausea. Since then, loud noises have been setting off dizziness: a slammed door, the TV turned up. Today the dizziness has been severe and she came in because it was not easing. No headache, no new hearing loss reported, no weakness, numbness, speech or vision change. No fever.

PMH: PTSD; mild TBI 2020; seasonal allergic rhinitis. PSH: ORIF right femur 2020; diagnostic laparoscopy 2020, negative.
Social: teacher, never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.

Exam: vitals reviewed, within normal limits. Anxious appearing. HEENT: otoscopic exam unremarkable bilaterally. Neck supple. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Neuro: alert and oriented, cranial nerves II-XII intact, strength and sensation normal, finger-to-nose normal. Romberg positive. Gait: has difficulty keeping her balance walking.

MDM: Vertigo with a clear pressure trigger (forceful nose blowing) followed by sound-induced vertigo. Picture fits a perilymphatic fistula. Neurologic exam otherwise nonfocal.

Impression: Vertigo; suspected perilymphatic fistula.

Disposition: discharged home, accompanied. ENT referral; follow up with primary care this week. Instructions: no nose blowing (dab only), sneeze with mouth open, avoid straining, bending and heavy lifting, head of bed up, no driving. Return for worsening vertigo, hearing loss, severe headache, weakness or vomiting that won't stop.

Seen in the ED 1/6 for vertigo; record reviewed.

About 10 days ago she blew her nose hard and the room spun, with nausea. Since then loud sounds bring the dizziness on; a pan dropped in the kitchen this morning did it. Following the ED precautions. No hearing change she has noticed. No headache. She is anxious about it and about going back to work Monday.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Anxious, comfortable at rest. TMs normal. Cranial nerves intact. Strength normal. Romberg positive, as in the ED. Walks carefully, a bit unsteady.

A/P
Suspected perilymphatic fistula (pressure event, then sound-induced vertigo). Urgent ENT/otology referral placed; front desk to push for first available. Continue precautions: no nose blowing, straining or lifting. Out of work until ENT sees her. Return or ED for hearing loss, worsening vertigo or neuro symptoms.

conditions.note: perilymphatic fistula after forceful nose blowing

reports.text: Pure-tone air and bone conduction thresholds within normal limits, 250 to 8000 Hz, both ears. No air-bone gap. Speech reception thresholds agree with pure-tone averages. Word recognition excellent bilaterally. Tympanometry type A bilaterally.

documents.title: Otology Consultation
documents.author: otolaryngology
documents.body:
Otolaryngology / Otology
Date of visit: 01/21/2026
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Dear colleague,

Thank you for sending Ms. Whitcomb, a 38-year-old teacher, seen in the ED on 1/6. On about 12/30 she blew her nose very forcefully and had immediate vertigo and nausea. Since then, loud sounds trigger dizziness. She has followed the ED's precautions and has been out of work. No hearing loss noticed. Background: PTSD, mild TBI in 2020, seasonal allergic rhinitis.

Exam: anxious but pleasant. Otoscopy: external canals and tympanic membranes normal bilaterally. Cranial nerves intact. Romberg positive.

Audiogram today: normal hearing thresholds in both ears.

Impression: perilymphatic fistula, diagnosed clinically from the pressure-related onset and sound-induced vertigo.

Plan:
- Conservative management: relative rest, head of bed elevated, no nose blowing, straining, bending or heavy lifting; sneeze with mouth open.
- Out of work for two weeks, through 2/4, then return as tolerated.
- CT temporal bones without contrast to exclude superior canal dehiscence.
- Recheck in about 6 weeks, sooner for any hearing loss or worsening vertigo.

Thank you for allowing me to see her.
Otology

documents.title: Work Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Ms. Whitcomb has been under medical care for an inner ear condition and is unable to work from January 7 through February 4, 2026. She may return on February 5, 2026, as directed by her ENT specialist.

reports.text:
Indication: sound-induced vertigo after a pressure event; evaluate for superior canal dehiscence.
Technique: thin-section axial CT of both temporal bones without contrast, with Poschl and Stenver reformats.
Findings: The superior semicircular canals are covered by bone bilaterally; no dehiscence. Posterior and lateral semicircular canals, vestibules and cochleae are normal. Oval and round windows unremarkable. Ossicular chains intact and normally aligned. Middle ear cavities and mastoid air cells clear. External auditory canals normal. Internal auditory canals symmetric and normal in caliber.
reports.conclusion: Normal CT of the temporal bones. No superior semicircular canal dehiscence.

documents.title: CT result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Abigail, your CT of the inner ears came back normal, with no thinning over the balance canals. ENT will go over it at your follow-up. Hope you're feeling steadier.

Otolaryngology / Otology
Date of visit: 03/04/2026
Re: Abigail Whitcomb, DOB 09/01/1987
Allergies: NKDA. Medications: none.

Dear colleague,

Ms. Whitcomb returns for follow-up of her perilymphatic fistula. She went back to teaching on 2/5. The dizziness with loud sounds faded over the first weeks of February and she has had none for several weeks now. Balance feels normal to her.

CT temporal bones 1/27 was normal, with no superior canal dehiscence; reviewed with her.

Exam: otoscopy normal. Gait normal, tandem gait normal. Romberg negative.

Impression: perilymphatic fistula, resolved with conservative care.

Plan: resume full activity. Gentle nose blowing, one side at a time, going forward. Follow up with us as needed if symptoms recur.

Otology
